evidence_detail: IDENTITY: InChIKey XEKOWRVHYACXOJ-UHFFFAOYSA-N regenerated from SMILES CCOC(=O)C with RDKit 2026.03.6 -> exact match; C4H8O2, MW 88.11, single component, a real liquid acetate ester. v04 SMILES CCOC(C)=O is the same molecule written differently. EPS PLAUSIBILITY: printed NBS514 p.12 (PDF idx 19) row 'Ethyl acetate ... 6.02  25  1.5  at 25  8,63,276' read directly from the held PDF (sha256 cb3fa923...). Back-extrapolating 6.02 from 25 C to 20 C with NBS's own printed coefficient a=0.0150/C gives 6.095, vs literature 20 C values 6.09-6.10 (delta 0.08%). Modern sources also tabulate 6.02 at 25 C. HOMOLOG SERIES (all four read from the same printed circular): methyl acetate 6.68 (25 C), ethyl acetate 6.02 (25 C), propyl acetate 5.69 (19 C), butyl acetate 5.01 (20 C) -> strictly monotonic decreasing. MA>EA by 0.66, i.e. 3.67x the quadrature of the two NBS 2% bands (0.180), so the MA>EA ordering the chemistry predicts (shorter chain, higher dipole number density) is robust to the stated accuracy. PHYSICS: Kirkwood-Froehlich g factor (formula validated on water g=2.81, methanol g=3.07, ethanol g=3.14) gives g=0.958 for EA, 0.972 MA, 1.011 propyl, 0.903 butyl - i.e. g~1, no parallel dipole correlation, no association, no ionic/water contamination signature. N*mu^2 falls 1.000/0.870/0.747/0.685 across the series, quantitatively explaining the whole eps trend by dipole density alone. PHASE: mp 189.55 K (-83.6 C), bp 350.25 K (77.1 C); 298.15 K sits 108.6 K above mp and 52.1 K below bp -> unambiguously liquid; NBS states pressure is atmospheric unless footnoted. TEMPERATURE PROVENANCE: judged a MEASUREMENT temperature, not a tabulation convention. NBS514 prints a per-substance t (13 distinct values in part 1: only 45/200 rows = 22.5% at 25 C, while 97/200 = 48.5% are at 20 C), and supplies a temperature coefficient with an applicability range; EA's range reads 'at 25', pinning the anchor to 25 C. The tabulated t is the anchor of the underlying measurement, and the successful 20 C back-extrapolation confirms 25 C is a real thermal state rather than a renormalisation. 298.15 K is the anchor itself, so ZERO temperature harmonisation/extrapolation is applied to this record. FREQUENCY: NBS514 sec.2 states values are 'intended to be the limiting values at low frequencies, the so-called static values' and that dispersion-affected data are excluded, with a footnote only 'in questionable cases'. Neither EA nor MA carries any frequency footnote (the f=3.6/4/5e8 footnotes belong to other rows), so both are static-class. Debye relaxation for acetate esters is at fr~30-47 GHz; at a 1951-era bridge frequency of 1 MHz the dispersion deficit is ~1e-9 of (eps_s - eps_inf), and at 10 kHz ~1e-13 - negligible versus the 2% accuracy class. Comparable to a modern zero-frequency value, with the caveat that 'static' is NBS's 1951 low-frequency-limit judgement, not a certified 0 Hz datum. PURITY: to inflate eps by +0.10 requires 0.138 vol% water (~1500 ppm mass, linear) or 0.68 vol% (~7500 ppm, Bruggeman); 1000 ppm water shifts eps by only +0.066 (linear) / +0.013 (Bruggeman), i.e. ~1% or less, so water is NOT a credible inflation route because eps only rises 6->80. The worse impurity is the hydrolysis co-product ethanol (eps 24.3, fully miscible): 5000 ppm -> +0.091, 10000 ppm -> +0.183 (3%). Contamination is therefore bounded to well under the 2% band by the <1% agreement with modern literature. CAVEATS (not chemistry, routed to provenance): v04's 6.02 is itself sourced from 10.6028/nbs.circ.514 at the SAME record nbs514:p20:022, so source_verification.csv's 'epsilon_agrees=true' is one transcription compared with itself, NOT independent corroboration; EA remains single-source. NBS lists refs 8, 63, 276 (all unbracketed = employed) and ref 63 (J.W. Williams & I.J. Krchma, JACS 49, 1676, 1927) is ALSO a primary source for methyl acetate, so EA and MA are not independent of each other. NBS accuracy class for a 3-figure value is 'probably accurate to 2% or better' (+/-0.120 on 6.02), i.e. class (b), not the 0.5% four-figure class. Chemistry and conditions are sound; admission still requires the provenance and independence reviews to clear the single-source/circularity issues.
